content.user_title: Plan newsletter revenue with clear assumptions
content.value_statement: Newsletter teams need a practical way to compare subscription and sponsorship revenue without hiding assumptions. This skill creates a labeled model, rate card, and growth projection from provided data.
actual_capabilities: Build paid subscription tiers with stated conversion and price assumptions.
Create CPM, CPC, or flat-fee sponsorship rate cards.
Project revenue at current, 25 percent growth, and 50 percent growth milestones.
Label inputs and outputs as Measured, User-provided, or Estimated.
Design referral, recommendation, or boost loops with explicit assumptions.
Check sponsorship labeling, claims, and commercial-mail consent gaps.
limitations: It needs list size, engagement data, or a revenue target to size a model.
It does not supply industry benchmarks as facts when source data is absent.
It does not calculate ROI, payback, or list value.
It flags disclosure and consent risks but does not provide legal advice.

use_cases.title: Launch paid tiers
use_cases.description: Compare paid-tier structures and estimate recurring revenue with transparent conversion assumptions.

use_cases.title: Sell sponsorships
use_cases.description: Turn open and click data into inventory, floor prices, and a sponsor-ready rate card.

use_cases.title: Plan a hybrid model
use_cases.description: Compare subscriptions, sponsorships, and growth loops across several list-size milestones.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic model
prompt_templates.prompt: Model monetization for my 12,000-subscriber newsletter. I want paid subscriptions and sponsorships. Our open rate is 38 percent.

prompt_templates.title: Create a rate card
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a sponsorship rate card for a weekly newsletter with 30,000 active subscribers, 44 percent opens, and 2.5 percent clicks.

prompt_templates.title: Compare revenue mixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare paid-subscription-only, sponsorship-only, and hybrid plans for a 45,000-person list. Use my 42 percent open rate and show every assumption.

prompt_templates.title: Build a growth scenario
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a 12-month newsletter revenue plan using paid tiers, two sponsorship slots, and a referral loop. Show current, 25 percent, and 50 percent list-growth scenarios.

output_examples.input: Compare paid subscriptions and sponsorships for a 20,000-subscriber weekly newsletter.
output: A paid-tier model with price and conversion assumptions clearly labeled.
A sponsorship inventory table with CPM and flat-fee options.
A revenue comparison at current and growth milestones.

output_examples.input: Create a sponsorship rate card using a 42 percent open rate.
output: A sellable impression base from active subscribers and open rate.
Primary and secondary placement options with floor prices.
A disclosure checklist for sponsored content.

best_practices: Provide active subscribers, send cadence, open rate, click rate, and current revenue before modeling.
Keep estimated conversion, fill rate, CPM, and growth assumptions visible in every projection.
Review sponsorship disclosures, claim support, and commercial-mail consent before selling inventory.
anti_patterns: Do not present estimated subscription revenue as measured revenue.
Do not use competitor rate cards as verified facts without checking their source and relevance.
Do not include subscribers without commercial-mail consent in the sellable audience.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide active subscribers, engagement rates, send cadence, current revenue, and your preferred monetization goal.

faq.question: Can this skill create a sponsorship rate card?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create CPM, CPC, and flat-fee options based on your stated audience and inventory.

faq.question: Does it invent conversion benchmarks?
faq.answer: No. Missing values are labeled as estimates or needs source rather than presented as facts.

faq.question: Can it calculate newsletter ROI?
faq.answer: No. It prepares revenue inputs and routes return, payback, and list-value math to a dedicated calculator.

faq.question: Does it connect to my email platform automatically?
faq.answer: No. It works with data you provide. Optional platform connections are not required.

faq.question: Does it provide legal approval for sponsorships?
faq.answer: No. It flags disclosure, claim, and consent issues for review, but it does not provide legal advice.
